name: Sentiment Variance
description: Measures the emotional volatility and fluctuation of sentiment across a document. Due to rigorous Safety and Alignment training (RLHF), Large Language Models are heavily conditioned to maintain a consistently polite, neutral, or mildly positive tone. They rarely exhibit sudden emotional swings, sarcasm, or pure negativity unless explicitly jailbroken. Human writers, conversely, are emotionally dynamic. A human essay might transition violently from frustrated critique to passionate advocacy, creating a highly volatile sentiment trajectory.
mechanism: The algorithm evaluates the sentiment (valence/arousal) of the text on a sentence-by-sentence or paragraph-by-paragraph basis using a sliding window. It calculates the statistical variance of these sentiment scores over the length of the document. A flat, unwavering sentiment line (variance near zero) strongly suggests the 'sterilized' and aligned output of an AI. A jagged, highly variable sentiment graph points to authentic human emotional expression and narrative arc.
useCase: Highly effective for analyzing reviews, personal essays, op-eds, and argumentative writing where human passion naturally causes structural shifts in emotional tone.
strengths:
• Exceptional at detecting standard, un-prompted LLM outputs, which are notoriously bland, diplomatic, and 'safe'.
• Analyzes the psychological footprint of the text rather than just its structural grammar, making it hard to bypass with simple paraphrasing tools.
limitations:
• Provides little signal on texts that are *supposed* to be emotionally flat, such as technical documentation, scientific papers, or financial reports.
• Can be bypassed if a user specifically prompts the AI with complex emotional instructions (e.g., 'start angry, then become hopeful').
parameters:
Analysis: Sentence-Level Sentiment Polarity Tracking
Metric: Variance ($\sigma^2$) of Sentiment Trajectory
Output: 0-100 Emotional Sterilization (Alignment) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 76-83% accuracy. It is an excellent psychological metric that beautifully complements purely statistical syntactic methods.

references.title: Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. arXiv.
Bhattacharjee, A. et al. (2020). Investigating the Role of Emotion in AI-Generated Text. ACL.
